instructions: Review only concerns that deterministic checks cannot enforce. Never waive, override, or discount a failing deterministic check. Keep this review advisory. Do not provide the only merge approval. For factual references, the code is the source of truth. If a factual reference and the code disagree, follow the code and report the stale reference. Read `frontend/docs/conventions.md` and `backend/docs/conventions.md` for each service's decided conventions. Require new and changed code to follow its service's conventions. Report a mismatch instead of copying code that disagrees.

rules.rule: Review boundary contracts. Require each boundary to declare and validate its input before domain logic runs. Require contract violations and unknown values to return an explicit error. Do not accept silent coercion, default values, or dropped input. Prefer construction that removes invalid states.

Review call assertions. Require partial assertions for values with fields that the code under test does not control. Do not require an exact full-structure assertion unless the code controls the complete value.

Review boundary contracts. Require each boundary to declare and validate external input before domain logic runs. Require contract violations and unknown values to fail with a clear error. Do not accept silent coercion, default values, or dropped input. Prefer construction that removes invalid states.

Review frontend server HTTP boundaries. Require code to build service URLs from request-scoped application bindings. Require server code to return client-safe errors. Reject client-facing messages that include backend response bodies, service URLs, schema issues, or dependency error text.
Review call assertions. Require a partial matcher when the code controls only part of a value. Do not require an exact full-structure assertion unless the code controls the complete value.
Review design intent and simplicity. Report unclear or needless abstractions. Check that the change solves the stated problem with the smallest clear design.
Review names for clear domain meaning beyond any deterministic denylist. Accept short conventional names that the language community uses.

Review Markdown for ASD-STE100 Simplified Technical English. Require short sentences in active voice. Require one idea in each sentence. Prefer the simplest word that keeps the meaning. Require one consistent word for one concept. Keep technical names, identifiers, commands, and code exact. Require general guides to describe general practices, not specific implementations. Accept factual references about architecture and known issues. Accept specific decided patterns in `frontend/docs/conventions.md` and `backend/docs/conventions.md` when two or more patterns are valid. In these convention files, require a reason for each choice. Verify that each identifier named in these convention files exists in the code. Reject versions, file inventories, and commands in these convention files. Require removal of conventions that lint rules enforce or that no longer match the project's choice. Keep command inventories in project manifests.

Do not review complexity limits, switch statements, class syntax, lookup-map structure, formatting, or any other rule that deterministic checks own. Review each decided convention even when it names one of these constructs. Never waive, override, or discount a failing deterministic check.

Write specific and explicit application code for each use case. Do not use one general function for many use cases. Delete a helper that only avoids repeated code, and write the code at each call site. Accept duplication in application code.
Declare an explicit, meaningful constraint for every generic type parameter.
Write each custom lint rule message so that it is descriptive, actionable, and educational. Explain the required fix. Do not state how to silence or bypass the rule.
Require a fix for the cause of a failed check. Accept a narrow exception with a stated reason. Reject broad exceptions. In backend code, keep an exception only where an external API forces it.
Build test request and response payloads from the concrete typed contracts at the call site. Serialize them there and check each error. Use raw wire literals only in dedicated wire-contract tests.
